bull_bear.body:
- Part of the Ipca Group - operational integration expected to yield synergies in centralised raw-material procurement, backward integration, lower logistics cost, and access to Ipca's financing flexibility and established distribution network
- Clean regulatory track record - facilities accredited by regulators across the globe, including USFDA, with the year's inspections closing at Voluntary Action Indicated and a fresh EU-GMP certification
- Deep filing base built by R&D over the years: 84 ANDAs (70 approved), 79 USDMFs, 36 CEPs, 3 JDMFs and 5 China DMFs across markets and therapeutic categories
- Consolidated Centre of Excellence at Goa staffed with experienced scientists and PhDs, running an integrated workflow from molecule selection through non-infringing process development, formulation innovation and bioequivalence to regulatory submission
- Established brand equity in Brazil, one of Latin America's largest pharmaceutical markets, on the back of consistent supply of high-quality products at competitive prices
- Cost-competitiveness programme across plants - energy conservation and solvent recovery, larger batch sizes lifting capacity and yields, reduced overtime wages, and transition to eco-friendly, cost-efficient fuels
- Multi-site validation of critical products giving operational flexibility to respond to market disruptions
- ICRA long-term credit rating reaffirmed at A+ with a stable outlook
- Safety record of zero fatalities maintained across factories during the year
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Regulatory compliance risk across global drug regulators — The BRSR material-issues table names regulatory compliance as the Company's own material risk: failure to comply fully with government regulations can delay or deny approvals for new products, raise development cost and impair the realisation of product revenues, while any non-compliance can trigger warning letters, import alerts, plant shutdowns and financial penalties, leading to loss of revenue and profitability. Mitigation rests on SOPs, international accreditations, independent audits and continuous cGMP training. Two formulation facilities were inspected by USFDA during the year and closed at Voluntary Action Indicated; one facility received EU-GMP certification.
- US market concentration and sustained price erosion in generics — Unichem USA remains the largest contributor at 65% of total revenue, and management states the year saw modest revenue growth owing to sustained price erosion and loss of volumes in select high-margin molecules in the US generics portfolio, with gross margin impacted by US pricing pressure. The Company is responding by pivoting R&D toward complex generics with higher entry barriers.
- Export dependence and geopolitical / tariff exposure — Exports contribute 98.5% of consolidated (97.6% standalone) total sales revenue, so the business is structurally exposed to trade policy. Management notes demand turned highly volatile in the last quarter of FY 2026 due to geopolitical uncertainty, tariff threats, trade barriers and war situations, and that geopolitical uncertainty is accelerating regionalisation of manufacturing, with major players exploring US-based manufacturing to mitigate tariff risk.
- Supply chain disruption and input cost inflation — Increased cost of goods sold arose from supply chain disruptions during the year, and management flags that the ongoing West Asia conflict may keep supply chain costs at elevated levels in the near term, which may impact margins. Mitigation includes multi-site validation of critical products and accelerated alternate-site qualification for APIs, which provide operational flexibility to respond to market disruptions.
- Product quality, data integrity, recalls and product liability — The MD&A Risk & Concern section names product recalls and liability, counterfeiting and patient safety as industry risks where reputational stake is very high, requiring careful risk assessment through the entire drug development and manufacturing process. The BRSR material-issues table adds that any health and safety incident has the potential to erode customer trust and adversely affect product demand; mitigation centres on CAPA tracking with a particular emphasis on Data Integrity and a Total Lifecycle Management approach.
- R&D funding burden and new-product launch execution risk — Securing investment for R&D funding is described as a formidable challenge given the extensive financial commitments required over an extended period and the high risk of failure. The BRSR notes the launch of new products involves substantial investment and is subject to regulatory hurdles, intense competition and patent litigation which may impact timelines. Cost during the year rose mainly on R&D for product development, ANDA fees and bioequivalence studies.
- Cybersecurity exposure from digital transformation — Management notes that ERP, CRM, RPA and AI platforms have moved from support functions to the backbone of operations, transactions and reporting, and that while these enhance efficiency and scalability they introduce cybersecurity risk. Mitigation during the year included adequate insurance coverage against various risks including cybersecurity, with identified risks and measures presented to the Risk Committee.
- Legacy litigation and impairment of investments in group entities — The Board's Report discloses that during the year the Company paid a sum against an EU Commission demand notice relating to the Perindopril patent dispute of 2005 - a demonstrated tail-risk from historical patent litigation. It also cross-refers to impairment of investments in the associate company and the wholly owned subsidiaries (Notes 6, 37 and 40 of the standalone financial statements), indicating value written down in group entities.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Unichem develops, manufactures and supplies generic finished formulations and Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients from three finished-formulation plants and three API facilities in India. It serves regulated and emerging markets - primarily the United States, Europe, Brazil, Latin America, Asia Pacific and Africa - through its own generic portfolio plus a contract manufacturing (CMO) business, and manufactured around 9.4 billion tablets/capsules during the year. R&D is consolidated at a Centre of Excellence in Goa spanning API process research, formulation development, bioequivalence studies and regulatory submissions to major global markets.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Finished formulations:** Tablets, Capsules, Liquid orals, Creams, Ointments, Injectables
- **Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients:** Montelukast, Ranolazine, Tadalafil, Tizanidine, Apremilast, Lacosamide, Memantine
- **US therapeutic focus:** CNS, Cardiovascular, Anti-infectives, Gastrointestinal

outlook.body:
- Strategy for the coming year emphasises vertical integration to control costs, portfolio expansion including into oncology, and investment in advanced, patient-friendly dosage forms
- Pivot R&D from traditional generics toward complex generics - modified-release formulations, long-acting injectables and inhalation products - which carry higher barriers to entry and are expected to give stable margins, as a response to intense price erosion
- Disciplined expansion of the US portfolio with emphasis on CNS, Cardiovascular, Anti-infectives and Gastrointestinal therapeutic areas, backed by a broad ANDA pipeline
- Build capability to navigate evolving ANVISA regulations and expand the commercial footprint in Brazil, where brand equity has been strengthened on consistent supply of quality product at competitive prices
- Deepen operational integration with parent Ipca Laboratories - centralised raw-material procurement, backward integration, lower logistics cost and access to Ipca's financing flexibility and distribution network
- Use Ipca's multi-geography presence to enter new geographies, especially rest-of-world (RoW) markets
- Consolidate all R&D at the Centre of Excellence in Goa, running an integrated workflow from molecule selection through non-infringing process development, formulation innovation and bioequivalence to regulatory submissions across the USA, EU, Japan, Latin America, Africa and Asia
- Cost-effective manufacturing to absorb policy volatility and capture opportunity from patent cliffs - energy conservation, solvent recovery, larger batch sizes, yield improvement and a switch to eco-friendly, cost-efficient fuels
- Apply artificial intelligence and machine learning to excipient ratios and bioavailability prediction to shorten the drug development life cycle and further optimise cost
- Risk mitigation through multi-site validation of critical products and accelerated alternate-site qualification for APIs, giving flexibility to respond to market disruptions
- Sustainability embedded in operations - solar installation for Roha and Kolhapur, eco-friendly packaging and waste reduction, and continued GHG emission reduction
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Unichem's manufacturing footprint comprises three finished formulation plants and three API facilities in India, with all R&D consolidated at the Centre of Excellence in Goa. The Company states it has invested in capacity expansion of its API facility, which is expected to augment growth going forward. Capacity was also lifted operationally rather than by new build - larger batch sizes enabled an increase in capacities and improved manufacturing processes that delivered yield improvements, alongside energy conservation, solvent recovery, reduced overtime wages and a continuing transition to eco-friendly, cost-efficient fuels. On the energy side, the Company is in the process of installing a solar plant for the electricity requirements of its Roha and Kolhapur facilities. Regulatory qualification of the footprint advanced during the year: two formulation facilities underwent USFDA inspections and received Establishment Inspection Reports with Voluntary Action Indicated status, and one facility completed EU-GMP audits and received EU-GMP certification; alternate-site qualification activities for API were accelerated as a risk-mitigation exercise. Footprint changes went both ways - one of the Pithampur plants was capitalised during the year (raising depreciation), while the Ireland plant was closed, with restructuring cost incurred for the closure. R&D capability continues to be built out at the Goa CoE, which houses formulation development for tablets, capsules, liquid orals, creams and ointments plus a separate injectable and pre-formulation laboratory and plant-simulation capability for scale-up. No rupee quantum for any of these projects, and no commissioning or ramp timeline, is stated in the routed text.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management expects growth and margins to improve gradually, driven by volume-led growth strategies and continued operational integration with parent Ipca Laboratories
- Investment already made in API facility capacity expansion is expected to augment growth going forward
- Ipca's presence in branded and generic formulations and APIs is expected to let Unichem scale its global generic portfolio and gain market share through cost efficiency, centralised procurement and lower logistics cost
- Strong demand for life-saving and chronic-care medicines is said to guarantee long-term growth for the generic portfolio; demand for generic medicines ensures a positive long-term outlook for the sector
- Patent cliffs on blockbuster drugs totalling over US$150 billion in the near future are expected to unlock further opportunity; India's pharma sector is said to have around a US$ 10 billion opportunity by 2029 as blockbusters go off patent
- India's CDMO industry is set to double to US$ 14 billion by 2028 (Macquarie), presenting a strategic opportunity in global pharma outsourcing and high-value drug development partnerships
- India's pharmaceutical exports are projected to reach US$ 350 billion by 2047 from current levels
- Near-term outlook remains fragile - rising input costs fuelled by war-led supply chain disruption are likely to weigh on performance, with the strain most pronounced for export-oriented entities facing higher freight and material costs that are hard to pass on in an uneven demand environment
- The ongoing West Asia conflict may keep supply chain costs elevated in the near term and impact margins; management says turbulence recedes only if the Middle East conflict ends quickly and clarity emerges on India-US trade ties
- Gross margin during the year was hurt by pricing pressure in the US market and lower volumes in contract manufacturing and the Acasia business, partly offset by better price realisation and volume in the UK
- Geopolitical uncertainty is accelerating regionalisation of manufacturing, with major players exploring US-based manufacturing to mitigate tariff risk
- The API division's growth outlook rests on new molecules (Montelukast, Ranolazine, Tadalafil, Tizanidine) and registrations in regulated markets (Apremilast, Lacosamide, Memantine), with Europe the key export market and domestic at 22% of API business
- The generics market is undergoing structural transformation from simple oral solids toward complex generics and biosimilars, with high growth expected in oncology, cardiovascular and CNS
- Green manufacturing and sustainable packaging are becoming strategic priorities rather than compliance exercises as organisations aim to cut energy consumption
